**Solution 1 (180) is invalid.** It assumes the tangents are parallel, but the configuration requires them to meet at a point X. Its own check gives PQ = 9, not 10, which it dismisses.

**Solution 2 (16√19 ≈ 69.7) is wrong.** Its setup is consistent, but its arithmetic does not check out.

**Solution 3 (≈ 521) has the right setup but a wrong result.** Its values cos α = 9/10 and sin α = √19/10 are correct. I verified them below. Its radii are wrong, and its final expression does not match the geometry.

**Independent check.** Put the homothety centre X at the origin with the bisector along the x-axis, and let α be the half-angle between the tangents. Since P and Q are symmetric about the x-axis, |y_P| = 5. The signed distances from P to the two tangents are u = x sin α − y cos α and w = x sin α + y cos α. Taking u = 3 and w = 12 gives y cos α = 9/2. With |y| = 5 this forces cos α = 9/10 and sin α = √19/10, and then x = 75/√19.

Each circle has its centre at (c, 0), and passing through P gives c²cos²α − 2xc + (x² + y²) = 0. This yields c = (150/√19 ± 12)/1.62. The tangent lengths from X are t_i = c_i cos α, so t = (150/√19 ± 12)/1.8. Their values are t₁ ≈ 12.45 and t₂ ≈ 25.78.

The quadrilateral U₁U₂V₂V₁ is a trapezoid with parallel sides perpendicular to the bisector. Its area is (t₂² − t₁²) sin α cos α. Here t₂ − t₁ = 40/3 and t₂ + t₁ = 500/(3√19), and sin α cos α = 0.09√19. So the area is (20000/(9√19)) · 0.09√19 = **200**.

None of the three proposed answers is correct. Solution 3 is the closest in approach, since its setup matches the correct geometry, so it is the most likely to be right among the three.

CHOICE: 3
